why_next: The TOST/CI approach resolves the parent's underpowered permutation test: CI upper bound 0.123 < delta=0.15 confirms orthogonality at < 2.25% shared variance on deterministic Flask mock, but fails at delta=0.10 (CI needs n ~ 865 vs current 480). The product-decision boundary is now bounded: delta=0.15 acceptable -> parallel channels justified; delta=0.10 required -> need more data or fused classifiers. However, all evidence remains on deterministic Flask 3.1.3 + PyJWT HS256 localhost with graded session_status_check. The critical unknown is whether real APIs with stochastic DB/cache/CDN, production middleware, and alternative JWT algorithms preserve the near-zero correlation structure. This requires materially different infrastructure (real API endpoints, not mock servers) and is the highest-upside question for C-FRESHNESS product deployment.

established: Behavioral-structural signal orthogonality confirmed at delta=0.15 on deterministic Flask 3.1.3 + PyJWT HS256 localhost: pooled r=0.0335 (r2=0.001), 95% CI [-0.056, 0.123], CI upper 0.123 < 0.15. TOST p_upper 0.005 at delta=0.15. Shared variance < 2.25%, > 97.75% independent. n=480 paired samples from 8 co-occurring conditions x 60.

TP/variance trade-off broken and verified across multiple experiments: graded session_status_check (401->1.0, 403->0.5, 500->0.75) with session_change=1 for ALL session_invalidation samples achieves mean TP=1.0 (Wilson lower 0.9398 > 0.75) across 8 co-occurring conditions while maintaining within-condition variance (8/8 conditions std>0 for both signals). FP=0.0 on 240 noise-only samples.

Power analysis established: for true |r|=0.05 at alpha=0.05, minimum n=1538 (permutation test). At n=480, minimum detectable |r|=0.0895. Observed |r|=0.0335 is below detectable threshold, confirming parent C3 failure was underpowering, not non-orthogonality.

TOST equivalence test is the appropriate methodology for very-low-magnitude correlations where the question is 'is |r| small enough?' not 'is |r| exactly zero?'. CI upper bound test replaces underpowered permutation p<0.05 gate.

Per-condition heterogeneity: SI+optional_field_addition r=-0.314 (p=0.014) is 1/8 expected under global null (expected 0.4 significant at alpha=0.05). Pooled r=0.0335 is the confirmatory measure. Permission_boundary conditions contribute zero behavioral variance (b_std=0 for PB conditions per raw_evidence).
rejected: Permutation p<0.05 as the sole confirmatory criterion for very-low-magnitude correlations (|r|<0.1) — provably underpowered at any practical sample size; replaced by TOST/CI equivalence test
Session validity randomization via 50/50 coin flip as a path to valid orthogonality test — achieves C2 variance but breaks C1 TP (mean 0.729 < 0.85) by creating false negatives
signing_key_rotation as a co-occurring drift pattern — blocks ALL endpoints, making structural signal unobservable
delta=0.10 achievable at n=480 with CI-based rule — minimum n=865 required (Fisher z TOST); min_n_tost values reported in result.json are ~4x too small and require correction

recommended_action: Test behavioral-structural orthogonality on real APIs with stochastic behavior. Design a graph lane experiment using real API endpoints (e.g., self-hosted production-like REST APIs with DB-backed responses, cache headers, CDN simulation) to measure whether |r| < 0.15 persists when: (a) behavioral signals come from real JWT validation, session state, and permission checks; (b) structural signals come from real schema/documentation endpoints; (c) stochastic variation is introduced via DB state, cache TTL, and timing jitter. If orthogonality holds at delta=0.15 on real APIs, C-FRESHNESS can advance toward VALIDATED. If orthogonality breaks (|r| > 0.3), the product must pivot to fused classifiers. Do NOT increase n to 865 for delta=0.10 confirmation until real-API orthogonality is established — the practical significance question (do real APIs preserve near-zero correlation?) is more important than the statistical power question (can we confirm delta=0.10 at larger n?).
